title: Impact of Scaling and Rounding on Metaheuristic Performance for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows
summary: Classical Euclidean instances for the Vehicle Routing Problem with Time Windows (VRPTW) have floating-point arc costs derived from node coordinates. This raises reproducibility and numerical consistency issues. Hence, a common practice is to scale and round data to integer values, yet the impact of these choices is poorly understood. This paper studies the effect of integer scaling by a factor P and compares three rounding schemes with distinct feasibility and optimality guarantees.
